blocked.title: Nonmonotone coverage under self-contained memory addition

audited.title: Nonmonotone coverage under self-contained memory addition

candidate.title: Nonmonotone coverage under self-contained memory addition

source_a.title: Towards a Formal Definition of Agent Memory: Basis, Span, Optimality, and the Sequential Memory Problem
source_a.claim: The formal memory framework assumes self-containment: storing an event never throws it away, and monotonicity: more memory is never worse, so coverage is non-decreasing in the stored set.

source_b.title: GeoForge: Non-Parametric Self-Evolving Agents for Earth-Observation Reasoning
source_b.claim: In GeoForge's retrieval sensitivity analysis, retrieving a small number of high-quality skills achieves the best performance, while excessive retrieval slightly degrades trajectory quality due to redundant guidance.

empirical_evidence.relation: The operational assumption that adding stored items cannot reduce coverage is violated in the same memory/retrieval setting when additional retrieved guidance is present but degrades trajectory quality.

lane_evidence.assumption: Coverage is non-decreasing in the stored/retrieved set because storing an event never discards it and more memory is never worse.
lane_evidence.violation: Adding more retrieved skills beyond a small high-quality set degrades trajectory quality because redundant guidance changes execution.
lane_evidence.scope_link: Both concern reusable procedural/experience memory used by an agent to answer or execute a task; source A formalizes memory coverage, while source B empirically varies the amount of retrieved memory and measures downstream planning quality.

candidate.irreducible_object: A coverage operator over stored procedural items whose answerability can decrease when an added item is retained, not merely a retrieval-quality or prompt-length effect.

mature_theory_baselines.name: Nonmonotonic logic / belief revision
mature_theory_baselines.same_information_projection: Treat the added skill as a new default rule that conflicts with prior rules and causes retraction of a previous conclusion.
mature_theory_baselines.reduction_test: This predicts conclusion retraction when conflict information is explicit, but source B attributes degradation to redundant guidance rather than an identified contradiction; the object is the retained-item coverage decrease under redundancy, not conflict resolution.

mature_theory_baselines.name: Information retrieval precision-recall / noisy-channel coverage
mature_theory_baselines.same_information_projection: Treat excessive retrieval as lower precision or noise, so expected answer quality falls with irrelevant items.
mature_theory_baselines.reduction_test: This requires the added items to be false or irrelevant; source A's self-containment says stored events are not discarded, and source B says the added guidance is redundant rather than false, so precision noise does not express the same retained-item monotonicity break.

same_information_nonreducibility.claim: The prediction is that a self-contained addition can lower coverage even when no stored item is removed and the added item is not independently false, because procedural items interact through execution redundancy.
same_information_nonreducibility.why_each_baseline_cannot_express_predict: Belief revision explains retraction from explicit conflict, not degradation from redundant retained guidance; precision-recall explains degradation from irrelevant/false items, not a self-contained true/redundant item that reduces coverage.

candidate.exact_prediction: For a fixed query and fixed prior memory M, there exists an added procedural item e such that M∪{e} retains every item in M, contains no negation of a stored event, yet has lower task-grounded coverage than M; the decrease is mediated by redundant execution obligations rather than deletion or false content.
candidate.strongest_same_information_baseline: Noisy-channel precision-recall with redundant items modeled as distractors.

domain_transfer_audit.why_not_domain_transfer: The candidate does not merely rename nonmonotonicity or retrieval noise; it targets a procedural coverage operator where self-contained, non-false additions reduce answerability through execution interaction.

rejected_patterns.reason: The veto applies when nonmonotonic reasoning or belief revision expresses the same retraction under the same conflict information. Here the observed degradation is attributed to redundant guidance, not an identified conflict or retraction premise, so the same-information baseline does not reproduce the prediction.
The evidence is not about sparse validation or filtering tradeoffs; it is about adding retrieved memory and observing degraded trajectory quality under a monotonicity assumption.
The candidate does not claim sharing helps in one population and harms in another under matched budget; it concerns adding retained items to one agent's memory/retrieval set.

source_a.evidence_excerpt: We assume \newtermmonotonicity (Assumption 11): more memory is never worse, so coverage is non-decreasing in the stored set.

source_b.evidence_excerpt: Retrieving a small number of high-quality skills achieves the best performance, while excessive retrieval slightly degrades trajectory quality due to redundant guidance.

semantic_reduction_review.lane_contract_reason: The lane contract requires the empirical violation to occur in a 'scope-linked setting.' Source A formalizes a mathematical generation operator in an abstract knowledge representation space where 'coverage is non-decreasing in the stored set.' Source B evaluates an LLM agent's trajectory quality degraded by 'redundant guidance' during retrieval. The violation is not empirically linked to Source A's specific generation operator or its defined answerability/coverage metric; it conflates an abstract mathematical assumption with an engineering retrieval bottleneck in a different system.
semantic_reduction_review.reason: The candidate attempts to bypass the 'procedural-memory-nonmonotonicity' veto by substituting 'redundant guidance' for 'explicit conflict.' However, in logic and information theory, redundancy is a form of monotonicity break under bounded computational resources: adding non-contradictory but redundant information degrades answerability by increasing execution/search complexity without adding net utility. This is already fully expressible by nonmonotonic reasoning under resource bounds or standard information retrieval precision/noisy-channel models, meaning no new structural prediction survives.

candidate.cheapest_problem_falsifier: Construct a controlled procedural-memory benchmark where each added item is true, non-contradictory, and self-contained; show that coverage/task success never decreases after addition after controlling for item relevance, false content, and prompt length.
candidate.endpoint_headroom_requirement: The problem remains open only if the decrease survives controls for false claims, explicit contradictions, prompt-length/cost, and ordinary retrieval precision; otherwise it collapses to noise or nonmonotonic belief revision.
